title: Upper bounds from the heart by left completeness
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal A),D(\mathcal B)$ and cohomology $H^j$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume countable products [def-weil-category-product] exist in both abelian categories and are exact, meaning that the product of every countable family of short exact sequences is short exact. Assume $D(\mathcal A)$ is left complete: for every $K$, the canonical maps $K\to\tau_{\ge -n}K$ make $K$ a derived limit of the truncation tower. Here $\tau$ denotes standard good truncation [def-kun-truncations], and a derived limit means a Roos triangle $L\to\prod K_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod K_n\to L[1]$, where the components of $s$ are the transition maps [def-weil-derived-limit]. Let $T:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ be an exact triangulated functor [def-weil-triangulated-category] preserving countable products with their projection maps. Let $\mathcal S$ be any class of objects of $\mathcal A$, viewed in degree zero, and let $c\in\mathbf Z$ satisfy
$$H^j(T(M[0]))=0\qquad(M\in\mathcal S,\ j>c).$$
Then for every integer $b$ and every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ such that $H^i(K)\in\mathcal S$ for every $i$ and $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$, one has
$$H^j(TK)=0\qquad(j>b+c).$$
No bound on the negative cohomological degrees of $K$, no lower amplitude bound for $T$, and no cohomological-dimension assumption on all objects of $\mathcal A$ is imposed.
